# MEDITATION II.

...the rights and boundaries of what he is about to describe. Truly, he who is not strong enough to perform this task will never be able to sufficiently remove all difficulties. If it is true anywhere, it is certainly most true here what the Apostle says: <note>original: "ἐκ μερȣς γινωσκομεν"</note> *we know in part.* Nor should anyone oppose me by citing the best and most pious men—for example, **Job**, **Jeremiah**, **Nathan**, and others—who, when weighed down by adversity, broke out into mournful voices and, seeing the flourishing state of the ungodly, often spoke with less reverence about the **Providence of God** <term>Providence: The protective care of God over the world and the belief that all events are divinely ordained.</term>.

For besides the fact that we do not deny that it can happen even to the best minds—even those touched by the greatest reverence for the Divine—that when pressed by various evils and mindful of their own innocence, they may indulge in grief beyond measure and deplore their sinister fates otherwise than is fitting; for as the poet **Phædrus** testifies:

> ->The spirit is with difficulty contained<-
> ->Which, conscious of its own sincere integrity,<-
> ->Is oppressed by the insolence of the wicked.<-

It must be known that the complaints of these holy men were mostly sudden, joined with love for the Divine. When a more serene state of mind returned, they were suffused with shame and groaned because, carried away by the excessive vehemence of pain and led astray by a mistaken judgment regarding the happiness of the wicked, they thought and spoke less modestly and piously about the counsels and ways of the most high Deity. 

The case of those of whom we are now speaking is entirely different. For these men burst into such complaints because they think too highly of themselves and their own merits. They take a singular pleasure whenever they can increase the difficulties occurring around this argument, or when they see them multiplied by others. They rejoice in their hearts if, having surveyed all the **Christian systems** <note>Referring to the various denominations and theological frameworks of the time.</note>, they find that not all doubts are entirely removed. For this reason, they chatter freely—that is, impudently—about the nature of divine administration, accusing both God and men, and repeating that an entirely different world ought to have been made. They do this not so much out of love for others whom they wish well, but rather from a desire for a happiness free from every blemish, which would last forever in this life. 

From this, it also happens that such men often regard the precepts of the Christian Religion—concerning patience, the love of enemies, the bearing of all kinds of calamities for the sake of Religion, the taming of wicked desires and emotions, and so on—as impossible and therefore contrary to all reason. Many examples of this are available; for instance, the famous **Uriel Acosta**, who, having rejected the Christian religion, had gone over to the Jews and afterwards gave his approval to the impious opinions of the **Sadducees** <note>A Jewish sect known in this period for denying the immortality of the soul and the resurrection.</note>; he could not stomach the command

<page-num>59</page-num>

of **Jesus Christ** regarding the loving of enemies. As is clear from the "theater of his life" <note>This refers to Acosta’s autobiography, *Exemplar Humanae Vitae* (An Example of Human Life), published posthumously.</note> added to **Limborch’s** friendly debate with a *Learned Jew*, Acosta was by nature eager for revenge. He would not forgive the Jews of Amsterdam by whom he had been poorly treated, judging this precept to be plainly impossible to fulfill and therefore unable to have God as its Author. 

Finally, I do not know whether those should not also be referred to this class who think that no opinions regarding religion should be subscribed to with firm mental assent unless they are entirely free from all doubts, exceptions, and difficulties. For that reason, they grieve vehemently that Christ and the Apostles did not work out the main points of Religion by a **mathematical method** <term>Mathematical method: A style of philosophy (more geometrico) that uses definitions and axioms to prove truths with the absolute certainty of geometry, popular among some 17th-century rationalists.</term>, but instead adorned their decrees, precepts, and examples in a certain popular manner. You would think these men never eat, drink, or move from their place unless they were led by geometric reasons! I am most firmly persuaded that if such a System had been given into our hands by Christ (to say nothing of other things that could be said here), they would have judged the Author of the Christian Religion even more insolently than they do now. Perhaps I shall not err if I say that men who judge in this way most clearly betray their impudent audacity and pride.

<margin>Love of pleasures and greed also usually cast men headlong into the vice of Unbelief.</margin>
**V.** Other affections follow, mostly drawing men away from true and chaste Religion: namely, the **love of pleasures** and **greed** (or avarice), which is the pursuit of money. Those who are devoted to the pleasures and delights of this life generally care little or nothing for those things which require industry and long examination to investigate. They are entirely fixed on those things which are pleasing and acceptable to the senses; meditations on weightier subjects and stricter disciplines are extremely troublesome and unpleasant to them. 

Since we are so constituted by nature that we willingly believe those things which harmonize with the affections of our minds, and since the Christian Religion insists that its disciples perform things that can in no way coexist with a soft and delicate life, it can easily be gathered how men devoted to their bellies and immersed in pleasures can fall into the vice of **Unbelief**. These precepts seem too harsh to them to be admitted, and they do not want to persuade themselves that God could wish them so much ill on account of a habit contracted in these vices. Hence, they think there is no reason why they should believe such a Religion to be of divine origin. Among those who frequent royal courts, follow military camps, and among the common crowd, the number of such people is very great.

# MEDITATION II.

...is the number. Yet there are such men among those who are thoroughly educated in the disciplines and who have examined the Christian religion with no small care. There are, for certain, many among the learned who follow the impulse of their passions rather than the decrees of Religion. It is established by experience that passions and sweet sensations have more power over the mind than even the weightiest opinions and arguments. 

These men willingly admit all the "theoretical" heads of Religion, as they are called, and they even frequently give their assent to foolish opinions; but when it comes down to the precepts for living rightly and piously, and when they hear that true happiness after this life is promised only to the diligent observers of these most holy commands—while infinite punishments will be imposed on transgressors—they begin to hate such a severe Teacher of what they consider to be very difficult morals. Driven by depraved desires, they cry out that it is scarcely credible that God has such great care for things done among mortals that He would so severely punish evil actions. They repeat that men are carried by nature toward all things that are pleasing; that the authors of such difficult precepts are not to be understood so literally, but rather their words should be interpreted in a more favorable way; and that perhaps the authors themselves, carried away by a certain fanatical and "hypochondriac" <note>In the 18th century, "hypochondriac" referred to a melancholy or depressive temperament believed to be caused by the organs of the upper abdomen.</note> temperament, turned away from delights which they had never tasted, and so on. 

To put it briefly, such men carry a mind that is entirely alienated from the Christian Religion for this reason. I do not think it necessary to show with more words how frequently, alas, men captured and bound by pleasures are accustomed to slip so disgracefully; no one who considers what goes on among men could doubt this. 

Thus (to add some examples), the **Reverend Father in Christ Gilbert Burnet**, formerly Bishop of Salisbury, describes **John Wilmot, Earl of Rochester** <note>Original: "Wilmotum Rosta Comitem"</note>—whose life, morals, paradoxical opinions on religion, and manner of death he described in a singular little book titled *The Repentance of the Earl of Rochester* <note>Original: "Rosta Comitis μετάνοια"</note>. He testifies that this most noble young man, endowed with outstanding talent, was first inflamed by the love of pleasures and thus proceeded toward such great impiety and unhappiness. From this, the same **Excellent Prelate**, having narrated the biography and the subsequent joyful—though very late—conversion <note>Original: "κατάστασει," referring to his state of mind or restoration</note> of this most excellent youth, warns young men and students of the best literature in the gravest words to beware in time of the love of pleasures, as it is the mother of Unbelief and Impiety, and a sinkhole of all evils. 

What the opinions and morals of **Hadrian Beverland** <note>A Dutch scholar known for his scandalous works arguing that "Original Sin" was actually the act of sexual lust.</note> were is not unknown to the learned; of him, we are given the opportunity to speak more diffusely elsewhere. Often these men, without beating around the bush, are accustomed to reveal what they truly judge regarding the most holy precepts of Jesus Christ.

# MEDITATION II.

...the number is not small. We now turn in a few words to *Avarice*. Anyone who rightly understands this passion and weighs the power it holds over the soul will concede that those suffering from this disease are easily led to a contempt for Religion. There are, to be sure, those who think that the Covetous fall more easily into the vice of vain *Credulity* and *Superstition* than into *Unbelief*. This latter point is true if we look only at the object toward which they are carried with all their might. Indeed, the care for "having" bites them so deeply, and they are so preoccupied and anxious about scraping together wealth, that they can hardly ever think seriously about matters pertaining to Religion. Thus, they "go where the path goes, not where they ought to go" <note>A variation of a common Latin proverb: *non quo eundum est, sed quo itur*.</note>; that is, they believe what is commonly said to be believed, and they subscribe to received opinions about Religion, though they have never examined them. Yet, notwithstanding this, they also easily rush into the opposite vice—namely, *Unbelief*. For besides the fact that those who do not care what they believe, or which articles of Religion they admit, should rather be said to believe nothing—for as *Seneca* <note>Lucius Annaeus Seneca, a Roman Stoic philosopher. The quote "He who lives everywhere, lives nowhere" (*qui ubique habitat, nullibi habitat*) refers to the lack of focus or commitment.</note> says: *he who lives everywhere, lives nowhere*—it must be noted that men burning with an insatiable desire for possession, and imbued with no certain principles of Religion, will easily surrender themselves to those who think basely of Religion if they see it is to their manifest advantage. To gain riches, they would seek heaven itself through folly. Even when dealing with the most sacred heads of Religion, they imitate *Terence's Gnatho* <note>Gnatho is a character from the play *Eunuchus* by the Roman playwright Terence. He is the quintessential "sycophant" or "yes-man" who flatters others for his own profit.</note>, whose creed of faith was this:

> *There is a class of men who want to be the first in everything,*
> *Yet are not: I follow these; I do not prepare myself so they may laugh at me,*
> *But I laugh along with them, and admire their wits at the same time:*
> *Whatever they say, I praise; if they deny it again, I praise that too:*
> *Does someone say no? I say no. Does he say yes? I say yes; finally, I have commanded myself*
> *To agree with everything; that is now by far the most profitable gain.*

Terence, *Eunuchus*, Act II, Scene II. Suppose a greedy man, equipped only with a superficial knowledge of the Religion received from his parents, enters into friendship with a wealthy, factious man—one who mocks Religion and is profane—who takes singular pleasure in the company of those who wish to mock the most holy things with "white teeth" <note>An idiom for mocking or laughing derisively.</note>. Suppose this same man perceives that great profit is brought to him by the familiar company of this person; can it be doubted whether that greedy man will compose his opinions according to the whim of this impious friend or not? Is it any wonder that a man who is not ashamed to cheat the Gods of their incense and weary heaven with filthy perjury would also cast his vote <note>original: "album adjicere calculum." This refers to the ancient custom of using white stones to vote for acquittal or approval.</note>

VI. Before we show by an induction of examples how many men—intent on following the winds of their passions and more violent commotions of the mind—have given their assent to the most pestilential opinions, I will put forward certain signs. From these, one can gather with enough probability whether a serious examination of Religion, or rather this or that powerless passion of the mind, moved a person to either attack or utterly deny the heads of our Most Holy Religion. Certainly, those who seem wise only to themselves, and who put much effort and study into stinging the most holy and weightiest articles of Religion—indeed, taking the greatest pleasure therein—can gather from these characters and signs (if they wish to judge the causes of their *Unbelief* seriously and from the heart) whether they would be doing something worthwhile and performing a duty worthy of a wise man if they were to apply their minds to a new, attentive, and serious examination of Natural and Revealed Religion.

These are the most powerful signs:
I. One who is endowed with no notable talent or erudition, and has not yet rightly understood and weighed the weightiest heads of Religion, yet at every given opportunity attacks and explodes the most momentous truths (which are not easy to grasp), must be said to be compelled to act this way by depraved passions, not by the decrees of reason.
II. Those who follow the wind of mere passions say and contend that all the Articles of Religion are unworthy of serious examination, and that it is all the same whichever Religion we uphold.
III. Those who, because of the differing opinions and sentiments into which the Christian world is (alas!) torn, say that all the heads of Religion are either uncertain or of equal weight, are obeying passions, not reason.
IV. He who wishes to believe only those things which agree amiably with his depraved inclinations, but treats the rest with a "high eyebrow" <note>A Latinism for disdain or arrogance.</note> of contempt, most manifesty betrays the levity and impotence of his own soul.
V. He who takes singular pleasure when he can mock and explode truths and opinions which, in the judgment of the wisest and most learned men, are not only evident but highly probable...

# MEDITATION II.

...rely on principles, but which can also contribute greatly to making people better in whatever state of life they are placed, follows not reason, but rather the wicked desires of the soul.

**VI.** He who indiscriminately rants against the Ministers of the Sacred, among whom there have always been—and still are—men excelling in learning, piety, and other virtues, and who accuses them without exception of both Superstition and Tyranny, wishing by that name to make Religion hateful to everyone, is an unrestrained buffoon and a wretched slave to the basest passions.

**VII.** Those who vehemently applaud themselves and rejoice in their hearts—consequently thinking meanly of Religion—when they notice the cause of Religion being handled poorly by this or that public Teacher, or its most holy dogmas being defended incorrectly, reveal their own intellectual immaturity and the manifest malice of their hearts.

**VIII.** Those who mock with a wide grin everything unusual found in the Sacred books of both Covenants <note>The "two Covenants" refers to the Old and New Testaments of the Bible.</note>, and wish to believe nothing except what approaches mathematical certainty, are listening not so much to the voice of reason as to the suggestions of their own emotions.

**IX.** Those who sharply defend opinions hostile to all Religion, but when asked again and again to first weigh the arguments of the most learned men opposed to these views before they give their firm assent to what they have once received, yet refuse to do so, are prevented by their passions from perceiving the truth.

**X.** He who defends, approves, and protects paradoxical opinions that are utterly abhorrent to Religion for the sole reason that they are rare, new, and unusual, has loosened the reins on his passions.

**XI.** Those who not only diligently read and study every book written by Unbelievers, but also extol their value with magnificent praise—while making nothing of all the other labors published in defense of Religion by the most learned men—belittling them as much as possible and shouting to their fellow-travelers that all their arguments are nothing but "straw," are mere actors. To such men, the largest possible dose of hellebore <note>Hellebore was a plant used in antiquity as a treatment for madness or insanity.</note> must be given immediately so that they might begin to be wise.

**XII.** Those who defend universal Skepticism or "Egoism" <note>In this context, "Egoism" likely refers to solipsism—the philosophical idea that only one's own mind is sure to exist.</note>, and strive to persuade others of it with many arguments, are swollen with foolish and ridiculous pride.

**XIII.** He who rejects and explodes the most serious and momentous truths of Religion, while at the same time being devoted to opinions that are either plainly foolish

and absurd, or at least less probable and likely than those he treats with such haughty contempt, is obeying the surge of his passions rather than the counsels of reason.

**XIV.** Those who maintain that there is a perpetual war between reason and revelation, and who so depress the powers of reason that they assert it is plainly blind and foolish in matters pertaining to Religion, are either fanatics or are deliberately trying to expose Religion to everyone’s mockery.

**XV.** Those who describe the lives and fates of Impostors or fanatics—such as *Apollonius of Tyana* <note>A Greek Neopythagorean philosopher from the 1st century AD, often compared by skeptics to Jesus to undermine the uniqueness of Christian miracles.</note>, *Muhammad*, and others—in such a way that they wrap their manifest follies and absurdities in silence, or studiously try to give them a favorable color, and who busy themselves confirming the fictional miracles and foolish sayings attributed to them with impressive oratory (for the purpose of detracting from the excellence of the Christian Religion and the divine dignity of our Holy Savior), do nothing else than reveal their own foolishness and daring impudence to all who have not been given a pumpkin <note>original: "pepo". These, unless I am mistaken, are the principal signs and indications from which those who wish to be called *Deists* can probably gather whether they have joined this faction out of a sincere pursuit of truth or not. The question is not whether others might err in this or that specific example (which we do not deny, and for that reason we warn everyone not to be headlong in judging the causes of errors). Rather, the discussion is whether most of those who declare war on Religion could not easily discover—if they wished to search the innermost recesses of their hearts and pay attention to these signs—that there is no reason for them to rest securely in their received opinions without a new examination, or to attribute their dissent from the views of other Christians solely to their own sharp wit and the cultivation of reason.

## MEDITATION II.

<margin>...defended. And first, indeed, this is proved by the example of the Jews living in the time of our Holy Savior <note>The author uses the Latinized Greek term "Soter" for Savior.</note>.</margin> ...that our thesis is wonderfully confirmed. We certainly do not wish to deny that Lucian, and many of the first Doctors of the Christian Church, often not only represented the opinions they were opposing incorrectly, but were even unfair to them. We grant, moreover, that the sublimity of the subjects to be understood, the misfortune of the times in which they lived, the preconceived opinions deeply fixed in their minds regarding the excellence and antiquity of their ancestral religion, and a lack of better counsel, hindered many from seeing more clearly into matters regarding Religion. All these things, I say, we willingly admit. Nevertheless, we contend that it was not so much the weakness of their talent or the difficulty of the subjects, but rather the **wicked desires of the soul** that were the cause of their failing to judge more correctly on such grave matters.

There are two points that clearly prove this: *The first* is that these men discussed other matters—which required no less sharpness of mind to understand—with great erudition and wisdom. In Italy and Greece, as is well known, there once flourished men of outstanding talent, sharpest wit, and great eloquence, well-trained in various disciplines. These men spoke most wisely and consulted most prudently on matters concerning the State in times of peace and war. Their words and deeds in these affairs are admired and looked up to by all who know how to give each thing its proper value. Yet these very same men, when they come to Religion and express their feelings about it, usually argue so foolishly that you would hardly believe such a vast difference in judgment could exist in the same individuals. Is it not credible that if these excellent men had wished to apply the edge of their talent and exert equal industry toward understanding the principles of Natural Religion <note>Natural Religion refers to truths about God that can be discovered through human reason and observation of the world, without relying on supernatural revelation.</note>, they would have judged more correctly?

The Apostle Paul certainly says, in the first chapter of the Epistle to the Romans, verse 28, speaking of the Pagans in general, and specifically of the Philosophers and Scholars among them: <note>original Greek: ἐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν Θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐγνώσει</note> **"they did not see fit to acknowledge God."** Anyone who deigns to read the meditations and testimonies of the most learned men on this first chapter of Paul’s letter to the Romans, and who is not a complete stranger to the history of philosophy, will be sufficiently shown how little these men cared for a pure examination of Religion.

*The second point* which leads us to assert that most were hindered by negligence and their emotions from judging Religion more accurately is this: they gave their approval to the most uncertain hypotheses—which cannot be compared in any way to the true principles of Natural Theology in terms of certainty and evidence—and defended them most fiercely whenever the opportunity arose. (*)

<column-break/>

## ON THE CAUSES OF UNBELIEF

But let us leave these men aside and speak of the people to whom God the Greatest and Best granted Revelation: namely, the *Jews* living in the age of Christ. When Christ, our most Holy Savior, came to the Jews to bring light (John 1:9) to a nation immersed in the thickest darkness of ignorance, their fate was very grim. This was partly because they had been reduced to the power of the Romans, and partly because the true decrees and precepts of Religion handed down by Moses and the Prophets had either been completely forgotten or so increased and obscured by the additions of new traditions that few—certainly not the common people, who are not usually concerned with the examination of Religion and follow the opinions of their Teachers and Leaders—could distinguish the genuine Oracles of the Prophets from the distorted explanations of the Pharisees. Even the writings of the Evangelists alone—to say nothing of the doctrines of the sects that were then prevailing among the Jews—more than sufficiently prove what I say.

Jesus, therefore, coming to bring a medicine, provided all those things that could have been very healthy for the sick, if they had wished to use the offered remedies correctly. To that end, he demanded not only that they abandon their previously accepted opinions about the special privileges of their Nation (Matthew 3:9; Luke 3:8; John 8:33 etc.) and suppress their pride, but also that they say farewell to the wicked desires of the soul. Hence *John*, about to prepare their minds to grasp heavenly Philosophy, repeated above all that great and divine demand: **"Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand"**; or: **"and believe the Gospel"**; as if he were saying (in the words of our great <term>Zwingli</term> <note>Huldrych Zwingli (1484–1531) was a major leader of the Reformation in Switzerland, known for his emphasis on the authority of Scripture.</note> on this passage): *those who wish to belong to Christ must, having laid aside their old life, begin a new one.* (Matthew 3:2; Mark 1:4).

By this saying, however, he did not mean that they should immediately agree before they had examined Christ’s teaching and miracles; but rather that, before all else, they should abandon those vices to which they had hitherto been addicted. This signified that they would only then be capable of receiving the decrees of heavenly doctrine and determining the true value of the discipline to be delivered by the Savior. This demand was certainly most *just* and most in accordance with reason. For besides the fact that a mind that is attentive, eager for truth, and free from wicked [passions is required to examine all kinds of truth...]

How shamefully most of the Jews despised this most healthy counsel is well enough known from the writings of the New Testament. Speaking generally about this matter, it was most true what our best Savior <note>original: "Soter," a Greek-derived term for Savior frequently used in formal Latin theology.</note> charged against the Jews in John 3:19–21, saying: *And this is the condemnation, that light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come into the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But he who does the truth comes into the light, that his deeds may be clearly seen, that they have been done in God.* 

Specifically, on the occasion of the miracles performed by Christ, it was clear that most were hindered not so much by weakness of mind, ignorance, and prejudiced opinions, but rather by the **most harmful stirrings and passions of the soul**. These prevented them from weighing those miracles as they ought, or from judging correctly regarding their nature, origin, and purpose. To be sure, these men accepted the Writings of the Old Testament and boasted in that name; they believed—and rightly so—that the miracles performed by Moses were of divine origin. They believed what is told of them in the Writings of Moses as firmly as if they had seen them with their own eyes, even though many centuries had passed since they were performed. 

However, when our Holy Savior, to prove his divine Embassy and to confirm his heavenly teaching, performed far more miracles than Moses did—performing them openly in the sight of both enemies and friends, and doing them in such a way that they could weigh all the circumstances of the event, and even appealing to them as infallible marks of a divine Mission—most of them either did not submit them to examination or replied that they would investigate the matter more deeply, yet held them as suspect. were to be attributed to evil demons, as recorded in Matthew 12:25. Can it not be clear to any sensible person from these examples (Compare John 9:8–34 and John 5:10 and following) that the causes of this slander or blasphemy are to be sought not in the difficulty of the matter being discussed, nor in mere prejudiced opinions, nor in weakness of mind, but in the **most harmful affections of the soul**? 

I believe no one would doubt this who considers not only these things, but also the other things said and done against the Holy Savior by these misguided men. Day and night they laid snares for him, so much so that he had to withdraw now to one place, now to another. Nothing had been said or done by him that these wicked hypocrites did not interpret in a sinister way; nor did they rest until they had delivered him to death, having cornered him with false slanders that were suspect even to a Gentile man—namely Pilate—who weighed them only on the scale of reason. 

After the Resurrection of the Savior (the fame of which remarkable and stupendous work they would have gladly extinguished), when the Holy Spirit had demonstrated in a clearly wonderful and unusual way that Jesus had been raised to the glory of the Father, and by that very work proved he wished to fulfill what he had promised his disciples, some from the insane crowd, incited by wicked speech, did not blush to attribute a matter most worthy of the attention of all people of sound mind and full of miracles to the effects of wine <note>A reference to the Pentecost account in Acts 2, where observers accused the apostles of being drunk.</note>.

If we proceed to the most holy teaching of Christ, it will be clear that they (we speak of the greatest part of that unhappy Nation and especially of its Leaders) wished to disparage it at every given opportunity. Most Jews thought correctly and magnificently regarding the law of Moses and the Oracles of the Prophets. We wish to detract nothing from their authority, for we acknowledge God as their Author. But if anyone compares the teaching of Jesus Christ with those, he will easily perceive—if he loves the truth—that whether we look at the excellence and clarity of the teaching itself, the weight of the arguments and incentives, or finally the duties and aids of every kind, it surpasses the Mosaic Religion by no small margin.

### MEDITATIO II.

...they could not appeal; partly because they overturned the very Laws of Nature. Our Savior <note>original: "Soter," a Greek-derived title for Jesus meaning "Healer" or "Preserver."</note>, when about to prove his doctrine or defend his deeds and words against the censures of the Jews, had appealed to Moses and the Prophets. But they, setting aside the oracles of Moses and the Prophets, opposed Christ or his disciples with nothing but **Traditions** when they intended to accuse them. See Matthew chapter 15:3 and following, and chapter 23:13–26. When, however, these crafty men wished to force him into their ranks, or to convict him of fraud, they were immediately reduced to silence upon hearing the response of Jesus Christ and the genuine interpretation of the law he brought forward; nor could they gain any protection for their Traditions from the law. 

Furthermore, they wished to utterly weaken the precepts known by nature and inscribed on hearts through the wicked interpretations which the unhealthy Scribes and Pharisees had devised. Thus, they thought the duties to be performed for parents could be evaded by rash vows. Matthew 15:5 and following; Mark 7:10–12. (**) For this reason, the most learned jurist **Barbeyrac** <note>Jean Barbeyrac (1674–1744), a famous legal scholar known for his work on natural law.</note>, in his elucidations on **Pufendorf's** <note>Samuel von Pufendorf, a 17th-century philosopher who wrote "On the Duties of Man and Citizen."</note> booklet *On the Duties of Man and Citizen*, most correctly states that this wicked interpretation was so contrived that it is manifest these men sinned against the clearest and most easily known decrees of conscience with deliberate effort. Jesus repeatedly insisted in John 4:24 that the true worship of the Divine must be sought in the innermost affections of the heart and the correction of the will and depraved stirrings; and the entire character of Christian discipline demands this very thing. 

The Jews, on the contrary—especially the leaders and Pharisees, swelling with empty pride—cared little for those things which pertained to the internal worship of the mind, but in observing external actions and rites, they were excessively diligent and superstitious. See John chapter 5:44; Matthew 23:13, 14 and following; Mark 7:3, 4; Matthew 6:5; Luke 8:12; and others, which among the moderns is discussed at greater length by **Basnage** (*History of the Jews*, Book II, chapter 2), **Le Clerc** (*Ecclesiastical History*, Prolegomena, Section I, chapter 2), and a great many others. They asserted that man was made for the sake of the Sabbath, rather than the Sabbath being instituted by God for the sake of man. Mark 2:17. ...ceremonial duties and traditions, as seen in the same 23rd chapter of Matthew. In this, the Jews were blinder than the **Gentiles** <note>Non-Jewish peoples, specifically the Greeks and Romans.</note> themselves, most of whom confessed that the true worship of the gods consists in purity of mind and innocence of life. Let us hear just a few testimonies from the great number of the Ancients. 

Thus **Cicero** says in Book II of *On the Nature of the Gods*: *The worship of the gods is best, and also the most chaste, most holy, and most full of piety, when we venerate them always with a pure, upright, and uncorrupted mind and voice.* For not only the Philosophers but even our ancestors separated superstition from Religion. **Pliny** in his *Panegyric* (chapter 4, section 6) says: *I notice even the gods themselves are delighted not so much by the elaborate prayers of those who worship them, as by holiness and innocence; and he who brings to their shrines a pure and chaste mind is thought more pleasing than he who brings a rehearsed poem.* Who is a stranger to the words of **Persius**, found near the end of his second Satire, where the Poet says:

> Tell me, high priests, what is gold doing in the sanctuary?
> Surely the same as the dolls given to Venus by a young girl.
> Why do we not give to the gods that which the bleary-eyed 
> offspring of Great Messala cannot give from a large platter:
> Justice and Law joined in the soul, the holy recesses 
> of the mind, and a heart steeped in noble honor?
> Let me bring these to the temples, and I will make my offering with a handful of meal.

Compare the commentary of the most learned **Casaubon** on this passage. He who requires more should consult **Huet**, **Grotius**, **Pfanner**, **Gataker**, and others who, by collecting testimonies from everywhere, have placed the matter in a clear light. 

Finally, if we weigh what the Jews judged concerning our Savior himself and his actions, it will be most manifest that most of them, seized by anger, envy, and evil zeal, wished to detract from his dignity in every way. All those who look upon the character, words, and deeds of both without bias <note>original Greek: "aneu pathon," meaning without passion or prejudice.</note> will admit that Moses can in no way be compared with our Savior. Yet they felt magnificently about the former, while most of them—certainly those masked actors, the Pharisees—despised the latter with a haughty brow, interpreted all his words and deeds in the worst possible way, slandered him, and laid snares for a life that had deserved well of them. The entire Gospel History teaches this. It will suffice to have brought forward one or two examples. The **Samaritans**, as is known, disagreed with the Jews on certain points of Religion, and for that reason, they were an abomination to them. Jesus, the gentlest Teacher, wished to call the Samaritans back to the right path by teaching better things, as seen from his familiar conversation with...

Furthermore, when his disciples—inflamed by a sectarian zeal and an improper, impious passion—breathed nothing but anger and vengeance against the Samaritans in Luke chapter 9, verse 55, he not only severely rebuked them but also simultaneously established that such hatred and the desire for vengeance against those who disagree is utterly foreign to the character and nature of his teaching, saying: <note>original: "ουκ οιδατε οιου πνευματος εστε υμεις"</note> "You do not know what kind of spirit you are of." Indeed, in the following chapter, through the parable of the Jewish man who lay dying and wounded by his injuries—shamefully neglected by his own "orthodox" brothers but treated with singular kindness and love by a Samaritan—he clearly showed that disagreement in matters regarding Religion ought not to prevent one person from doing good to another. 

Yet the Jews were so far from taking these most reasonable and equitable warnings to heart, or from judging more correctly, that they instead called the Savior himself <note>The Latin text uses "Soterem," from the Greek word for Savior/Healer</note>, who deserved no such thing, a *Samaritan*—that is, to speak in the style of our own age, they called him a *most pestilential Heretic* in John 8:48. Regarding this, the most learned Berlin Interpreters <note>Refers to the Huguenot scholars in Berlin, Beausobre and Lenfant, who produced a famous French translation and commentary on the New Testament</note> note on this passage: <note>original: "C'étoit une des plus grandes injures que pussent dire les Juifs, c'est-a-dire, vous êtes un Heretique, un Schismatique, un Ennemi de la Religion, & de la Nation."</note> "It was one of the greatest insults the Jews could utter, meaning: you are a Heretic, a Schismatic, an Enemy of the Religion and of the Nation." 

When he forgave sins at the same time as he freed people from grave illness, they accused him of blasphemy in Mark 2:7. If he occasionally stayed with tax collectors and sinners and ate with them—in order to recall men captured and bound by wicked pursuits and passions to a sounder mind—they called him a "glutton," <note>The Latin "caenipetam" suggests a parasite or "table-chaser."</note> one who pretends to be like the virtuous Curius but lives like a reveler at a Bacchanalia, as in Matthew 11:19. When they noticed that he omitted certain minor rituals, such as the washing of hands before a meal, the Hypocrites cried out that the most sacred laws were being trampled underfoot by him in Matthew 15:2. When he provided immediate help on the Sabbath day to a man suffering from a grave illness and near to collapse, this seemed a crime worthy of death, or at least a deed from which any prudent person might conclude that he was moved by no reverence for Divine Law. In short, they omitted nothing that they thought could render him hated or make his most holy discipline suspect. From this, if I am not mistaken, it is manifest that most of the Jews who resisted the Religion delivered by Christ "with hands and feet" <note>A Latin idiom meaning to resist with all one's might.</note> did not sin out of a weakness of intellect, nor were they driven headlong merely by prejudiced opinions, but rather they proceeded to such madness and impiety for the most part because of the worst of passions. VIII. Which things we had said concerning the Jews living in the time of Christ can be applied in large part to the circumcised <note>original: "recutitis," a term for Jews referencing circumcision</note> of our own age. We admit, of course, that the Jews living in our Savior's time were bathed in a greater light and were driven, as if by a certain necessity, to receive the Messiah by so many miracles performed in their sight—miracles subject to no doubts—but because of the inflexible stubbornness of their minds, they are worthy of greater punishment. Meanwhile, notwithstanding this, we assert, and if I am not mistaken, rightly so, that most modern Jews are prevented from giving their name to the Christian Religion by the wicked pursuits of their souls. 

To be sure, the obstacles to the conversion of the Jews are not unknown to us. We know that the severity of certain Rulers under whose command they live, the violence and oppressions of the Inquisition, the dissensions and mutual brawls among Christians, their degenerate lives, the distorted methods used to try and convert that miserable Nation, the deadly hatred of most Christians toward them, and certain dogmas accepted among Christians, etc., contribute much to confirming those men in the opinions they have once soaked in. We are not ignorant of all these things, but confess them with sorrow. 

Meanwhile, if we turn our mind on the one hand to the arguments by which the truth of the Christian Religion is usually proved, and on the other hand to the powers of intellect required for the examination of these arguments, we see no reason why we should assert that modern Jews are of such dull intellect, or so stupid, that they cannot perceive the force of the reasons militating in favor of the Christian Religion. # MEDITATIO II.

...all Jews are completely unfit for weighing matters of somewhat greater investigation in a just balance. We know that there are not a few men among them endowed with no contemptible talent. Certainly, that famous Jew <note>This refers to Isaac Orobio de Castro (c. 1617–1687), a Sephardic physician and philosopher</note> with whom the celebrated **Limborch** <note>Philippus van Limborch (1633–1712), a Dutch Remonstrant theologian</note> exchanged the sword-blade of disputation, showed clearly enough what those people are capable of, provided they are willing to weigh matters pertaining to the stricter disciplines—especially Religion—with the same <note>original: "Ζηλω" (zelō)</note> zeal and study they usually devote to earning their bread or scraping together money. Whatever the case may be, it can be shown clearly enough that the arguments supporting the truth of the Christian Religion are far more evident than those which move the Jews to stubbornly cling to their current way of life—I will not say to opinions snatched up here and there through tradition, but even to the Religion once received from Moses and the Prophets. This itself shows more than enough that most are hindered by perverse prejudices from giving their name to the Christian Religion. Come, let us demonstrate this in a few words, since these matters have been discussed at great length by the most learned men: **Basnage**, **Stanhope**, **Kidder**, **Limborch**, and others. There are *three* principal points by which modern Jews are moved (notwithstanding the miserable state into which most have been cast) to give their approval to the Mosaic Religion and hold it as a divine Revelation. *First* are the miracles performed of old by God through Moses for the sake of the Jewish nation. *Second:* the fulfillment of Prophecies. *Third* and finally, the <note>original: "αυθεντια" (authentia)</note> authority of the Books of the Old Testament and the antiquity and certainty of the Tradition concerning the origin, state, and Religion of the Jews.

Regarding the Miracles of Moses, we hold them to be divine just as they do. But we contend at the same time that Christ not only performed more than Moses had done, but also gave his disciples the same power of performing miracles. We prove that Christ existed on earth and performed miracles in the same way that the Jews are accustomed to argue that Moses once lived among the Israelites and was famous for miracles. But this being granted, the question is: why do the Jews admit the Miracles of Moses performed so many centuries before the birth of Christ, yet reject the stupendous <note>original: "τερατα" (terata)</note> wonders of Christ? If we look at the nature of historical faith, there is no fundamental reason why they should deny that those things took place; for the more recent a narrative of an event is, and the less remote from the times in which we live, and the more witnesses there are of different character, religion, and location, the more all people of sound mind are accustomed to believe them. And if those witnesses are <note>original: "αυτοπται" (autoptai)</note> eyewitnesses, inflamed by a zeal for faith, piety, and integrity; if the remaining circumstances of persons, rituals, place, etc., agree with the things themselves that are reported to have been done,

the highest degree of probability arises from there. If all these things are observed in the examination of whether it is no less certain that miracles were truly performed by Christ our Holy Savior than by Moses, I am most fully persuaded that all impartial observers will confess that the reasons militating for the Christians are far more evident than those which can be brought forward by the modern Jews. If we proceed to the Prophecies and their fulfillment, we acknowledge again that Moses was a distinguished Prophet, and that Holy Men endowed with the gift of prophecy flourished among the Jewish people even before the birth of Christ, being <note>original: "φερομενους ὑπο πνευματος ἁγιου" (pheromenous hypo pneumatos hagiou)</note> "carried along by the Holy Spirit," and that the Jews do rightly if they open their eyes to the light kindled by them. But first of all it is well known (to say nothing of the obscurity of many prophecies, the lack of historical records, and the prophecies concerning the conversion of the Gentiles) that the Jews acknowledge there exist in Moses and the Prophets most famous oracles concerning the future Messiah. Since, however, they contend that he has not yet come and they repudiate Christ—and prophecies are only proven by the outcome—it is manifest that the Jews themselves are unfair toward Moses and the Prophets; and much of the strength of the arguments sought from the Prophecies is lost. If, however, we look back at the oracles of Moses and the Prophets which concern either the fate of the Jewish people or of other Nations, any sensible person and lover of truth, skilled in the matters under discussion, will be bound to confess that those oracles—whether you look at the express words or the outcome—can in no way be compared with the evidence inherent in the Prophecies predicted by Christ. The men praised shortly before have demonstrated this to the eye. See the celebrated **Limborch’s** *response to the third writing of the Jew*. Even **Josephus** <note>Titus Flavius Josephus (37–c. 100 AD), a Romano-Jewish historian whose writings are often used by Christians to verify New Testament history</note> alone is sufficient to confirm the prophecies uttered by Christ. Therefore, either Prophecies confirmed by the outcome are not a certain sign of the divine origin of Moses and the Prophets, or that sign must be attributed with much greater right to the prophecies of Christ. Since, however, modern Jews admit the oracles of the prophets as divine but reject those of Christ, it is manifest that they are driven by perverse prejudices to reason so preposterously.

Finally, if modern Jews appeal to the constant tradition concerning the glory of Moses and the writings of the Old Testament to prove the truth of the Jewish Religion, there is no reason for us to object: we confess that the Holy Man Moses died more than 4,000 years ago; we confess that the subsequent Prophets appealed to him; nor are we ignorant...

# MEDITATION II.

## ON THE CAUSES OF UNBELIEF

...we [know] that his fame is spread far and wide among the Nations; we detract nothing from his glory, even if we consider as a fable what some more recent Jews tell of him—as the **Illustrious Buxtorf** <note>Johannes Buxtorf (1564–1629) was a celebrated Hebraist who studied Jewish customs and language deeply.</note> testifies in his *Philological-Theological Miscellany*, page 197—namely, that God **by kissing the soul out of the body of the one about to die like a garment, and after death called him back to life, and he now serves God in the heavens.** <note>The author is referencing the Jewish tradition of "Death by a Kiss" (mitat neshika), particularly associated with Moses.</note> But here too the Jews are clearly blinded by love for their Sect, unless they admit that the fame of our Savior, and the writings of the New Testament, rest upon far firmer foundations (we speak of those who wish to conduct some accurate examination of these matters), and that the fame of our Religion was spread more quickly throughout the world. 

We are not ignorant that the *most learned man P. D. Huet* <note>Pierre Daniel Huet (1630–1721), Bishop of Avranches, was a renowned scholar who argued that pagan myths were actually distorted versions of biblical history.</note> wished to prove, with testimonies sought from every side, not only that the fame of the name of such a great Man [Moses] reached the most ancient nations living before the times of Christ, but even that *Moses* lies hidden under the fables of the Gods and Heroes—to say nothing of *Croese's Hebrew-izing Homer* <note>Gerard Croese (1642–1710) wrote a book claiming the Odyssey and Iliad were based on biblical stories.</note> and other books of similar metal. But that the most celebrated Bishop [Huet] used testimonies that were doubtful, uncertain, and indeed often suspected of being false to prove that last point, was shown in a singular and very learned dissertation by the *Most Learned James Hase* <note>Jakob Hasæus (1691–1723), a professor at Bremen.</note>, called to join the many [the dead] alas! in the very flower of his age, which exists in the *Bremen Library, Class VI, Volume V*. 

Whatever the case may be, it is clear enough that in this part too, Christians can contend on equal terms with the Jews. The fame of our Savior, since he appeared on earth, and the Religion delivered by him, was brought early to both Jews and Gentiles. The four Gospels were spread among the common people before the destruction of Jerusalem, as witnessed by *Irenaeus, Book III, chapter XI*, and by Tertullian throughout his books *Against Marcion*. The writings of *Clement, Barnabas, Hermas, Polycarp, and Ignatius* testify to the same. The Apostles had traveled early enough through the most noble provinces of the Roman Empire, intending to commend the heavenly discipline to all. Many Gentiles joined the Christian Religion: there exist the testimonies of *Pliny, Tacitus, and Suetonius* concerning Christians. Early on, violent persecutions were stirred up against them, in which the blood of the followers of Christ was indeed copiously shed, but besides the glory and fame of Martyrdom, the excellence of the most divine discipline was made known to many nations. That most famous letter of *Pliny the Younger* given to *Trajan*, of which *Tertullian* also makes mention in his *Apology*, is a monument more lasting than bronze <note>original: "aere perennius," a famous phrase from the Roman poet Horace meaning something immortal.</note> both of the faith and the very great number of Christians of that age. I pass over other things which could be brought forward here, and which long ago by learned men...

<column-break/>

...have been brought forward. (*) If then (to summarize our words) a constant tradition concerning Moses and his writings, and their uninterrupted preservation, wins them credit and proves their authority, then those things which Christians have thus far handed down concerning Christ and the Apostles, and their most ancient and certain writings, must also be admitted. 

But if anyone should ask what the cause might finally be why the Jews—whom some care for Religion touches, and who approach the examination of these matters with some effort of intellect—still most constantly adhere to the Jewish Religion despite these arguments, and despise the discipline of the Christians though it is fortified by greater defenses, I can respond with nothing else, having duly weighed all things, than that this must be attributed not so much to the difficulty of the matter as to the perverse affections of the soul. 

Besides these things, there are also others which show that the more recent Jews, by deliberate effort, do not wish to see the force of the arguments militating for the Christian Religion. I shall say nothing of the modern Religion of the Jews itself, which teems with many fables and foolish opinions; nothing of the ceremonies and rites contrary to rational worship (**), but I shall make mention of only two reasons...

---

(*) Nor do those things stand in the way of our words which were argued by the *Illustrious Vitringa* <note>Campegius Vitringa (1659–1722), a prominent Dutch theologian known for his work on synagogue history and prophecy.</note> in his *Sacred Observations, Book X, Chapter VII*, concerning the "languishing" state of the Christian Church from Nero to Trajan; certainly they do not prove that the number of Christians decreased. *Of the time*, he says on page 964, *that passed in the interval of thirty years from Nero to Trajan, we have only a maimed and sterile sacred history, which nevertheless, if the Church had flourished throughout all that time, ought to be memorable, and highly commendable for the abundance and variety of deeds, and for its usefulness:* But this argument proves nothing. 

First, we can say that writings of that kind have perished. 

(2.) Men living among fierce bears, and expecting most present death at every hour, scarcely had time for committing to letters those things which were worthy of remembrance and transmitting them to posterity. What *Sallust* <note>Gaius Sallustius Crispus (86–35 BCE), a Roman historian.</note> had said of the most ancient Romans—namely, that **all the best among them preferred to act rather than speak, and to have their own good deeds praised by others, while he himself preferred to tell of others' deeds** <note>The author is adapting a quote from Sallust’s *The Conspiracy of Catiline*.</note>—can, with a few things changed, be applied to the Christians of that age. 

(3.) The testimonies concerning the progress of the Christian Religion by *Eusebius, Tertullian, and Pliny* prove enough and more that a great daily addition was made to the nascent Church in those times: for where did such a great number of Christians under Trajan, Hadrian, and the Antonines come from, if they had been so greatly diminished from the last years of Nero until Trajan? 

(4.) Finally, the persecutions themselves and the Martyrs under Nero and Domitian prove that the Christians were increased daily. Let us take a middle path between the opinions of *Dodwell* <note>Henry Dodwell (1641–1711), an Anglo-Irish scholar who controversially argued that the number of martyrs in the early church was actually quite small.</note>, fighting for the fewness of the Martyrs of that age, and the common opinion strenuously defended by *Ruinart* <note>Thierry Ruinart (1657–1709), a French Benedictine monk and scholar who compiled historical accounts of the martyrs to prove their large numbers.</note>, and thus it will be clear enough that the number of Christians was not small, nor were many frightened away by persecutions from constantly giving their name to the most holy discipline. I pass over other things that could be brought forward here.

(**) Learned men have proven these things at length, *Buxtorf* in *The Jewish Synagogue*, *Eisenmenger* <note>Johann Andreas Eisenmenger (1654–1704), whose book *Judaism Unmasked* was a highly influential, though deeply hostile, critique of Jewish tradition.</note> in *Judaism Unmasked*, and others.

## ON THE CAUSES OF UNBELIEF

...of the reasons which make it manifest that the Doctors of the Jews and the Rabbis are seized by the worst affections of the soul when they rise up against the Christian Religion. The first is that they prefer to devise silly, ridiculous, and entirely untrustworthy little stories—or rather fables—about the origin, birth, miracles, and death of Jesus Christ, rather than to test the truth and divine origin against the Lydian stone <note>The "Lydian stone" or touchstone was a tool used in antiquity to test the purity of gold; here it refers to using reason as a standard for truth.</note> of reason through an accurate and established examination of the Christian Religion. Especially well-known are two horrible and accursed booklets entitled:

->**The Book of the Generations of Jesus of Nazareth**<-
<note>original: "Sefer Toldot Yeshu Ha-Notzri"</note>

One of these was published by the illustrious *Altdorf Philologist, Wagenseil* <note>Johann Christoph Wagenseil (1633–1705), a Christian Hebraist who published Jewish anti-Christian polemics to refute them.</note>, which appears in the second part of the book titled: *The Fiery Darts of Satan*. The other was shared with the learned world by that most celebrated man, *Johann Jakob Ulrich, Minister of the Word and most deserving Professor of our Gymnasium*, who was snatched away from all good men—and certainly from me—by a premature death a few years ago. Whoever reads those futile booklets will easily perceive not only that they are composed of mere lies and are poorly stitched together, but are so constructed that no one but a fool could be deceived by them; yet, among those people, such booklets are held in great value. The *second* reason is that many among the Jews, who chase after some praise for their erudition and wisdom, bestow much credit upon the **Philosophical Cabbala**. This, as is well known, is derived from the ancient Pythagorean-Platonic philosophy and has been augmented by certain Jewish commentaries. It is still a matter of dispute among the learned whether this system, if properly looked into, involves mere *Spinozism* <note>The philosophy of Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677), often accused by contemporaries of being a form of atheism or pantheism.</note> or not. Indeed, very plausible arguments can be brought forward on both sides, a matter which we deal with extensively elsewhere. But whatever the case may be, it is certain that this philosophy—sublime in appearance—is built upon no certain foundations; it is inept, fashioned entirely to foster Enthusiasm <note>In the 18th century, "Enthusiasm" referred to religious fanaticism or the irrational belief that one is receiving direct private revelations from God.</note>, and so filled with the delusions of a foolish imagination that most Jews, captivated by the love of this Cabbala, do not know what sense or power to assign to its obscure words. In a word, it is mere darkness compared with the most enlightened <note>original: "fanatissima," likely a typo for "sanctissima" (most holy) or "clarissima" (brightest), given the context of "darkness."</note> discipline of Christ. If anyone doubts this, I would wish him to unroll the collection of many such trivial works published under the name *The Cabbala Unveiled by Knorr von Rosenroth* <note>Christian Knorr von Rosenroth (1636–1689), whose "Kabbala Denudata" was a major source for Christian scholars studying Jewish mysticism.</note>; he will no longer doubt what I have said. Why is it, then, that the Jews despise the discipline of Jesus Christ—which is far easier to grasp, more agreeable to reason, supported by far stronger testimonies and arguments, and far better suited for perfecting the human mind—while they value those difficult absurdities so highly and commend them so greatly?

<margin>The same truth is confirmed by the example of many Heretics, who in the time of the Apostles and the following age attacked the Christian Religion.</margin>

IX. Before I move to more recent times and prove, by the induction of the most manifest examples, that *Unbelievers* have declared war on the Christian Religion driven by depraved affections—while conversely giving their approval to the most inept and uncertain opinions—something must be noted regarding the *Heretics of the Apostolic Age* and the age immediately following, as well as the Pythagorean-Platonic Philosophers who nitpicked at the Christian Religion. All who have examined the most ancient monuments of ecclesiastical writers with some care will admit that many of the Heretics, who in the first centuries after Christ's departure wished to disparage the Christian Religion, cherished opinions that were clearly inept and absurd. When weighed against the laws of right reason, these can in no way be compared with the dignity and excellence of the decrees of the Christian Religion. I know that the opinions of Heretics were often poorly understood and represented by the Church Fathers; I am not ignorant that quite a few things were falsely attributed to them, and that dangerous conclusions were often drawn from obscure principles and sold as their genuine sentiments. We are bound to admit all these things if we love the truth. And from this it is also clear how difficult it is to have properly perceived the mind of the ancient Heretics. I shall say nothing of the defenses of erudition with which those who wish to apply their minds to explaining the dogmas of the most ancient Christians and Heretics ought to be equipped. I note only this one thing: that very few judge the Heretics and their opinions **without passions** <note>original: "ἄνευ παθῶν"</note>, but for the most part they err either in *excess* or in *defect*. Some, by a deliberate effort, wish to interpret the clearly depraved actions of Heretics in a better light and to provide some color of legitimacy even to the most inept opinions. Others, however, whose number is far greater than the first, think they have satisfied their duty in this area only if they go in the opposite direction entirely. These people often offer us specters <note>Ghosts or imaginary monsters.</note> instead of men. All Heretics, if you listen to these critics, are either completely stupid, foolish, and dull-witted, or they are impudent, blasphemous, and contaminated by every vice. Every little fable and rumor must be believed when it concerns Heretics, for it is deemed "just" to hate such pestilential men. It is not considered impious to lie when acting against them, or to interpret the most innocent things poorly. The error of a Heretic, against which human nature is little guarded, must be called fatal; but the most shameful vices of those who attacked them must be cloaked and hidden by every art.

# MEDITATION II.

## ON THE CAUSES OF UNBELIEF

When dealing with their false opinions, one must never say that they arose from weakness or laziness, but one must cry out that everything is full of most deadly ambushes. Innocent opinions are, through the twists and turns of logical consequences, to be transformed into the gravest Heresies; ambiguous meanings are to be snatched away in the worst possible sense, and so on. This sin of skewing things in either direction by both ancient and more recent writers is too well known to be proven by many examples. Nevertheless—and this is the good fortune of our Century—there is no lack of excellent Men who show how these deviations are to be avoided. Among them, I must rightly mention the Reverend, Distinguished, and most Learned Author of the *Critical History of Manichaeism and the Manichaeans*, published in two volumes in quarto; namely, the most Learned *Beausobre*, <note>Isaac de Beausobre (1659–1738) was a French Protestant pastor and scholar famous for his massive study on Manichaeism.</note> who is **now among the Saints** <note>original Greek: "τον νυν ἐν Ἁγιοις" — a traditional formula for someone who has died.</note>. I certainly wish that all those who apply their minds to recounting and explaining the dogmas of the most ancient Heretics would keep this most learned Writing before their eyes. For he weighs and examines all things so learnedly; he represents the principles and conclusions of the ancients so incorruptibly; he detects the sources of errors so clearly and sharply; he judges the weight of errors so freely and yet modestly; he so guards himself against party zeal, the love of a Sect, and excessive reverence for the Church Fathers; in a word, he weighs everything according to the eternal laws of truth and equity, so that this work must rightly be numbered among the most excellent books published in our Century. 

We know, indeed, that the incorruptible judgment and candor of this most learned Man greatly displeased the disciples of **Ignatius Loyola** <note>The founder of the Jesuits.</note>, the compilers of the **Memoirs of Trévoux** <note>original: "Commentariorum Trivoltiensium" — a famous Jesuit literary and scientific journal of the 18th century.</note>. But besides the fact that the distinguished Man himself stoutly defended the first part of the work against the most unjust censures of the **Jesuits** <note>original: "Lojolitarum"</note>, and doused them with **Attic salt** <note>original: "sale attico" — a term for refined, sharp wit or sarcasm.</note> as they deserved, it is common knowledge that nothing is less a matter of care or heart for those good fathers than **the Truth**. It is almost **morally impossible** for these men to be able to offer a sincere judgment on the outstanding efforts of Learned Men who have seceded from the Roman Church, especially when it concerns matters regarding Religion. 

However (to return to the path), although it cannot be denied that the opinions of Heretics have often been poorly represented by both ancients and moderns alike, it is also certain—and can be called into doubt by no one who is even slightly versed in these Literatures—that many of the Heretics were so carried away by party zeal that, having rejected the clearest points of Religion, they defended monstrous, foolish, and hostile opinions against the most holy Religion. 

It is not, however, my intention to wander too far into this more patient field, or to laboriously weigh the dogmas of the most ancient sects,

<column-break/>

# 81

## ON THE CAUSES OF UNBELIEF

or to discourse at length on the life and morals of the Heretics. This has been done abundantly by most learned Men, whom those eager for these things may consult. Rather, I will confirm my thesis with only a few select examples sought from the first Centuries. It can be proven by the most certain testimonies that party zeal, hatred of others, and especially pride and ambition drove many of the most Ancient Heretics headlong; this is evident from the entire discipline they followed and their method of disputing against Christians. 

To be sure, these men had for the most part approached the examination of the Christian Religion after being imbued with the principles of Platonico-Pythagorean or Oriental Philosophy (which did not differ much from the former). However, that "horrid simplicity" which shines forth in the Writings of Christ and the Apostles offended minds filled with I-know-not-what sublime—or more rightly called chimerical—opinions. Hence, they either abandoned the Christian Religion entirely, or at least they wanted to reconcile it with their own hypotheses. This being the case, it was all the same to them whether they reached the end they intended through fraud and malice or by some other way. Let us take one or two examples. 

*It is well known what a monstrous System of Theology Valentinus and Mani, among others, constructed, and something will be said of this below.* That pride and ambition contributed much to the construction of such systems has been proven by Men most versed in Ecclesiastical history and most skillful explorers of character. The celebrated **Mosheim** <note>Johann Lorenz von Mosheim (1693–1755), an influential Lutheran church historian.</note> judges **Valentinus** thus in his *Ecclesiastical History, page 141*: *I am certain, he says, that the pride with which the wretched man burned (according to the testimony of Tertullian in his book against the Valentinians, chapter IV), since he was previously of strong intellect, disturbed his brain and cast him into a kind of mental illness.* For no sane person would believe that such insane fabrications could proceed from a sane man. He had conceived a hatred for the Christians, by whom he thought an injury had been done to him; and while he wanted to avenge this with a monstrous propagation of doctrine, his arrogant nature could not bring itself to swear by the words of others. Therefore, having retained the general principles of Philosophy, he devised a completely new arrangement of things; he increased the number of **aeons** <note>In Gnostic systems, Aeons are the various emanations or "powers" of God.</note> and ordered them differently, and invented new names for them. *In short: he attempted all those things which a disturbed mind, cast down from its status, is accustomed to plot.* So says **Mosheim**. 

**Epiphanius** <note>A 4th-century Bishop of Salamis known for his "Panarion," a massive refutation of heresies.</note> and many of the Ancients testify that **Marcion** joined the faction of **Cerdo** because he failed to obtain the Roman Bishopric when it was vacant after the death of **Hyginus**. Regarding **Mani** <note>original: "Manete"</note>, such things are told by the ancients that persuade me the man was an Impostor and clearly swollen with empty pride. Even the most learned **Beausobre**—who otherwise strenuously defends Mani where something seems inconsistent with the truth either to himself or his hypotheses—

Those who say that he retired into a cave where he composed his Gospel, and that he then boasted of having brought it from Heaven, make him an Impostor. But those who tell us that he received his Mission in a dream or in an Ecstasy seem rather to make him a Fanatic—at least if it is true that the Dream or Ecstasy were not faked. I do not wish to decide this question, especially since it is not impossible to combine these two characters. A man who begins with Imposture can very well end with fanaticism and persuade himself that he is indeed what he wanted to be.* To me, to tell the truth, it seems more probable that **Manes** was swept away toward defending such monstrous opinions by pride and ambition rather than by some lapse of a sound mind. This is evident from what the Ancients tell us about him. He was a man not only gifted with excellent natural talent, but also well-educated in various disciplines, especially philosophy. In the *Acts of Archelaus* <note>A 4th-century anti-Manichaean work attributed to Hegemonius, which presents a fictionalized debate between Mani and Bishop Archelaus.</note> on page 89, it is said of him: <note>original Latin: "Eruditus secundum omnem doctrinam..."</note> *He was learned in all the teaching found in those places, and I might almost say beyond any other man.* The most learned men, Abbot *Renaudot* in his *History of the Patriarchs of Alexandria* and *Assemani* in the *Oriental Library*, testify to the same. Indeed, if *Herbelot* and *Abulpharajus* are to be believed, he was not only trained in the sacred scriptures from childhood, but was even a Priest. *Manes* interpreted the Holy Scriptures and disputed strenuously against the Magi, the Pagans, and the Jews. *Beausobre* cites the actual words of these most learned men in Volume I, pages 83 and 158 following. In the same place on page 94, by bringing forward the testimonies of the ancients, it is shown that *Manes* not only despised the other Teachers of the Christian Religion as unrefined and simple, but also boasted that he would answer all proposed questions most accurately and untie all knots and doubts—which is a most evident sign of a very proud and vain mind. Is it any wonder, then, that men of this sort use frauds and lies to become more famous? Hence, when the *Distinguished Hottinger* the Elder, in *Ecclesiastical History Vol. I, page 147*, teaches from an Arabic manuscript that *Manes* asserted he had been called by God during a period of rest, and because—as *Renaudot* and *Herbelot* prove from Oriental records—he hid himself away in a cave and persuaded his disciples that he was going to be caught up into heaven and remain there for a year, and when that same period of time had elapsed, he spread among the public a certain Gospel under the name of a *Revelation* heard in heaven; hence, I say, any prudent person

<column-break/>

any prudent person will be able to gather that *Manes* fell into such madness not so much through some enthusiasm, but rather through a **most foul ambition**. The same could be said of most of the *Gnostics*, <note>A diverse group of early religious thinkers who claimed "gnosis" (secret, salvific knowledge) and often held dualistic views of the world.</note> the Heretics of the Apostolic age. For these men claimed for themselves some sort of secret discipline; they looked down on the Apostles with a high brow as if they were unrefined, and these most arrogant men babbled that they had obtained minds from the "intelligible world." See *Irenaeus*, Book I, chapter XXV, pages 103, 104, and Book III, chapter V, page 179 of *Massuet's* edition.

<margin>The same is shown from other signs.</margin>
X. But there are also many other signs from which it is clear that many of the Heretics of the first centuries were corrupted by ambition and pride. To this you may refer: II) that on one hand they were not ashamed either to reject the sacred books or to corrupt them and twist them to fit their own opinions; and on the other hand, they attributed forged books to Holy or Famous Men, such as *Zoroaster, Abraham*, and others. These facts are too well known for me to prove with many testimonies; it is enough to have brought forward only one or two examples. Thus *Clement of Alexandria* reports in *Stromata Book II, page 457* that the Gnostics rejected the Epistles written by Paul to Timothy, because Christians used them to defeat their opinions. *Tertullian*, in *Against Marcion Book V*, is witness that Marcion refused to admit the *Acts of the Apostles*, the Epistles to Timothy, to Titus, and to the Hebrews, because they were contrary to his opinions. The same *Tertullian* testifies in *Book IV, chapter 4* that certain passages of the Gospels and Epistles were corrupted by that same heretic, as being contrary to his views. The *Distinguished Beausobre*, in *Critical History of Manichaeism Vol. II, Book VIII, chapter 3*, proves in a whole chapter, citing the testimonies of the Ancients, that the *Manichaeans* attempted the same. It is well known that they likewise spread many fictitious books among the public under the names of Holy and Famous Men. Lest I be too long, I refer the reader to *Fabricius’s* <term>pseudepigrapha</term> <note>Writings falsely attributed to a historical or religious figure to give them authority.</note> collections of the Old and New Testament, *Beausobre’s Critical History of Manichaeism Vol. I*, *Mosheim’s Major Institutes of Christian History*, *Germonius*, and others. Let it suffice for us to bring forward one testimony, namely that of *Irenaeus*, in *Book I Against Heresies, chapter XX, page 91*, speaking thus: <note>original Greek: "Πρὸς δὲ τούτοις ἀμύθητον πλῆθος..."</note> *Moreover, they bring forward an unspeakable multitude of apocryphal and spurious writings, which they themselves have forged, to strike the simple-minded with amazement.* Do these things not prove more than enough that those men deliberately wished to insult the Christian Religion?
